questions.q: What is the key difference between a SharePoint list and a SharePoint library in Power Automate?
options: A list is faster to query than a library
A list holds structured rows with named columns; a library holds actual files
A library can only be read, never written to, by a flow
There is no difference — both terms describe the same connector surface
questions.explain: A list holds structured, column-based rows (the same shape as a database table), while a library holds real files such as documents or photos. Power Automate exposes different triggers and actions for each.

questions.q: Castlebridge Logistics wants a flow to start the instant a dispatcher logs a new row in the Shipping Exceptions list. Which trigger fits?
options: When a file is created in a folder
Recurrence
When an item is created
Manually trigger a flow
questions.explain: "When an item is created" watches a specific SharePoint list and fires in real time the moment a new row is added — exactly this scenario.

questions.q: Which SharePoint action would you use to pull back only the open exceptions assigned to a specific route?
options: Create item
Get items, with a filter query
Check in file
Delete item
questions.explain: "Get items" retrieves rows from a list and supports a filter query, so you can return only the rows matching a condition like route or status.

questions.q: A flow needs to add a signed incident report document to a SharePoint library after an exception is approved. Which action does that?
options: Create item
Update item
Create file
Get file content
questions.explain: "Create file" adds a new document to a SharePoint library. "Create item" is the list equivalent for adding a row, not a file.

questions.q: Why might a single Castlebridge Logistics flow use both a SharePoint list trigger and a SharePoint library action?
options: Because SharePoint requires every flow to touch at least two connectors
Because a list change (a new exception row) can trigger the flow, while a library action (filing the resolved document) finishes the work
Because libraries cannot be used with triggers at all
Because list actions are deprecated in favor of library actions
questions.explain: Lists and libraries serve different purposes in the same process: the list row starts the approval, and once it's resolved, a library action files the supporting document — one flow spanning both.
